Comparisons

Compare GLP-1 medicines

Most GLP-1 brand names come down to a few molecules: Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy all contain semaglutide, and Mounjaro and Zepbound both contain tirzepatide, so brands that share a molecule differ in approved uses, forms and doses.156 These pages set the medicines side by side, one pair per page, and two head-to-head trials compare tirzepatide with semaglutide directly.1112

The molecules behind the brands

Many GLP-1 brand names lead back to a few molecules. An FDA safety notice from 2024 lists the approved GLP-1 receptor agonists. The list starts with Byetta (exenatide) in 2005 and runs through Victoza and Saxenda (liraglutide), Trulicity (dulaglutide), Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy (semaglutide), and Mounjaro and Zepbound (tirzepatide).1 These drugs mimic GLP-1, a hormone from the intestine, to trigger insulin release and lower blood sugar after a meal.1 Tirzepatide also activates a second hormone receptor, the GIP receptor.5 Since that list, FDA has approved Foundayo (orforglipron), a daily tablet from Eli Lilly, on April 1, 2026, and Wegovy now also comes as a tablet.103

Molecule US brands What the labels cover
Semaglutide Ozempic (injection and tablets), Rybelsus, Wegovy (injection and tablets)143 Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular risk (Ozempic, Rybelsus), plus kidney risk (Ozempic injection); weight and cardiovascular risk (Wegovy), plus the liver disease MASH (Wegovy injection)243
Tirzepatide Mounjaro, Zepbound1 Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular risk (Mounjaro); weight and obstructive sleep apnea (Zepbound)56

Brand against its own ingredient

Four pages compare a brand with the molecule inside it: Ozempic vs semaglutide, Mounjaro vs tirzepatide, semaglutide vs Wegovy and Rybelsus vs semaglutide. In each pair the brand contains the molecule it is set against, so the active ingredient is the same. What changes is the approved product and its label: the same tirzepatide is approved for type 2 diabetes as Mounjaro, and for weight reduction and sleep apnea as Zepbound.56 Several of these pages also explain what the brand name does not cover, such as compounded or counterfeit products.

GLP-1 against a single drug

Two pages start from the hormone itself. GLP-1 vs semaglutide covers a drug that shares 94% of its sequence with human GLP-1 yet has a half-life of about one week.2 GLP-1 vs Mounjaro answers whether Mounjaro counts as a GLP-1 drug at all, since tirzepatide's label names two targets, the GIP and GLP-1 receptors.5 For the class as a whole, read What is GLP-1?.

Same molecule, different brands

Ozempic vs Wegovy and Ozempic vs Rybelsus compare products that all contain semaglutide. The differences are approved uses, doses and forms. Ozempic injections top out at 2 mg a week,2 while Wegovy injection's usual maintenance dose is 2.4 mg a week, with a label maximum of 7.2 mg.3 Rybelsus is a once-daily tablet of 3, 7 or 14 mg, and it is not interchangeable milligram for milligram with Ozempic tablets.4

Different molecules

Mounjaro vs Ozempic, Mounjaro vs Wegovy, Ozempic vs tirzepatide and Mounjaro vs semaglutide set tirzepatide against semaglutide. Two head-to-head trials anchor them. In SURPASS-2, 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes took weekly tirzepatide (5, 10 or 15 mg) or semaglutide 1 mg for 40 weeks; HbA1c fell 2.01 to 2.30 percentage points on tirzepatide vs 1.86 on semaglutide.11 In SURMOUNT-5, 751 adults with obesity and no type 2 diabetes took tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg or semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg for 72 weeks; average weight change was -20.2% vs -13.7%.12

Victoza and Saxenda

Liraglutide is an older GLP-1 drug that Novo Nordisk markets under two names, Victoza (approved 2010) and Saxenda (approved 2014).187 The split mirrors the newer drugs. Victoza is injected once a day; for adults the label starts at 0.6 mg for a week, then 1.2 mg, with a maximum of 1.8 mg.8 It is approved for type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older, and to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.8 For adults, Saxenda steps up each week from 0.6 mg to 3 mg a day from week 5.7 It is approved for long-term weight reduction in adults and children 12 and older who weigh more than 60 kg and have obesity, and in adults with overweight and at least one weight-related condition.7

Liraglutide has no comparison page of its own, but it appears in two trials covered elsewhere on this site. In STEP 8, a 68-week trial of 338 adults with overweight or obesity and no diabetes, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg led to more weight loss than daily liraglutide 3.0 mg: -15.8% vs -6.4%.13 In a 26-week trial of 711 adults with type 2 diabetes, semaglutide tablets 14 mg (a Rybelsus strength) lowered HbA1c by 1.2 percentage points vs 1.1 for liraglutide 1.8 mg, a result the label calls non-inferior.4

How to read these comparisons

Each comparison opens with a table: what the product is, its active ingredient, maker, form, approved uses, dosing schedule and first US approval, with a citation in every cell. Label facts come from the FDA labels cited on each page, as checked in October 2026. Trial numbers are averages from named studies. A head-to-head trial, where both drugs were tested in one study under the same rules, says more than numbers from two separate trials, and the pages point out which is which. Doses shown are label schedules for prescription products, and the prescriber sets the dose for each patient.

Frequently asked questions

Are Victoza and Saxenda the same?

They contain the same active ingredient, liraglutide, and both are daily injections from Novo Nordisk, but their labels differ.78 Victoza, at up to 1.8 mg a day, is approved for type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older, and to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.8 Saxenda, at 3 mg a day, is approved for long-term weight reduction in adults and children 12 and older who weigh more than 60 kg and have obesity, and in adults with overweight and at least one weight-related condition.7

Are Ozempic and Saxenda the same?

No. Ozempic contains semaglutide and is approved for adults with type 2 diabetes; Saxenda contains liraglutide, a different GLP-1 receptor agonist, and is approved for weight reduction.27 Ozempic injection is given once a week and Ozempic tablets once a day, while Saxenda is injected once a day.247 In the STEP 8 trial of 338 adults without diabetes, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg led to more weight loss than daily liraglutide 3.0 mg: -15.8% vs -6.4% over 68 weeks.13 That 2.4 mg dose is a Wegovy dose; Ozempic injection tops out at 2 mg.32

Which GLP-1 medicines share the same active ingredient?

Several brands are pairs or trios built on one molecule. Semaglutide is in Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy; tirzepatide is in Mounjaro and Zepbound; liraglutide is in Victoza and Saxenda; and exenatide is in Byetta and Bydureon BCise.1 Brands that share a molecule still differ in approved uses, doses and forms, which is why several pages here compare a brand with its own ingredient.

Is there a GLP-1 pill?

Yes, several. Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets are daily semaglutide tablets for adults with type 2 diabetes.4 Wegovy tablets, also semaglutide, have a 25 mg daily maintenance dose and are approved in adults for long-term weight reduction and to lower cardiovascular risk.3 Foundayo (orforglipron), from Eli Lilly, was approved on April 1, 2026, as a once-daily tablet for long-term weight reduction that can be taken with or without food.109 All of them are prescription medicines.34910

Do these pages say which medicine is better?

No. They report label facts and trial results, and they flag which results come from a head-to-head trial. In SURMOUNT-5, for example, 751 adults with obesity and no type 2 diabetes had an average weight change of -20.2% on tirzepatide vs -13.7% on semaglutide over 72 weeks.12 A trial average does not decide what suits one person. Choosing a medicine and its dose is a decision for the patient and prescriber, and these pages are not medical advice.
